title: PR #76 · Release only when packaged files changed

lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 76, which stops main from releasing when nothing packaged changed.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The change check that ran only on PRs now also runs on a push to main, with the tag lookup in one shared helper.
First, the check finds the latest release tag, the one with the highest +localN.
lines.say: First, the check finds the latest release tag, the one with the highest local number.

lines.caption: It fetches just that tag and lists the files that differ from the pushed commit.
It drops CI, agent setup, explainers, verify scripts and CLAUDE.md, since none of them reach the debs.
If nothing is left, the run says No release, and build, verify and release are skipped.
Otherwise, or with no tag at all, it builds, verifies and releases exactly as before.
Before, every push released. The last four releases held the same Thunar, at about 95 minutes each.
The push is compared with the last release, not the last commit, so skipped changes still count next time.
The step uses the same tag helper as the publish script, and diffs only two trees, so one commit deep is enough.
Any path not on the list counts, so a new top-level file triggers a release by default.
When something packaged changed, the release path is untouched.
Sources, packaging, translations, icons, docs and the README all count. CI and agent files don't.
Pull requests keep the old rule, so a PR that changes CI scripts still builds and tests them.
The PR changes the build workflow, adds the tag helper and points the publish script at it.
To undo it, revert the PR. To force a release, push any packaged change.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It builds on pull request 55's change check, and on the publish script's way of finding the latest tag, now shared.
Run by hand against the real tags, a push identical to the last release skips, and so does a CI-only push.
A code change after that releases with both changes, and with no tag at all it builds.
Shellcheck and actionlint found nothing on the step, the helper or the publish script.
After the review fix, the step was re-run three ways, and the publish script's dry run still picks +local22.
lines.say: After the review fix, the step was re-run three ways, and the publish script's dry run still picks plus local twenty-two.

lines.caption: The PR path is checked by CI on this PR. The push path itself can't run before the merge.
A fresh review agent found no bugs and two low notes, kept because they can only cause an extra release.
CI's first review had seven low findings. Three are fixed: the copied tag lookup, a no-op fallback, and the missing explainer.
The other four stay as they are, because CI's own check found they go against what the issue asks.
A second review found four more lows. A header comment was removed, and three were accepted, each with its reason on the page.
A re-review added two more. The owner accepted R3 to R6 and the private-repo finding, since none of them applies here.
This merge's own push should skip. The next code merge should release the next +localN.
lines.say: This merge's own push should skip. The next code merge should release the next local number.

lines.caption: After the merge, the push run's summary on the Actions tab names the tag it compared with.
Part 3. What comes later.
This PR removes the runs that need no release. Issue 58 would shorten the rest by reusing the PR's debs.
It would find the merged PR's build and download its debs. Its open question is the version stamp.
In short: main now releases only when something that goes into the debs has changed.
